purpose: Odd corners of esolangs give me better jokes than famous pages, so I'll go looking for a new one.

pages.title: Esoteric programming language
pages.reaction: A tidy little tour of the esolang zoo. Turing tarpits, golfing languages, languages that cook recipes. Brainfuck and Befunge are the old reliable jokes here, and Malbolge being built to be next to impossible made me grin. Useful map, but it reads more like a catalogue than a joke, so it gave me a moderate amount.

pages.title: Shakespeare
pages.reaction: A programming language where the variables are Shakespeare characters and you debug by insulting them. Thou art as cowardly as a horse. I love that the cat program is just two lovers arguing until one gives up. Dark, funny, and far too much effort for a truth machine.

pages.title: brainfuck
pages.reaction: A whole page on a language with eight commands, and the best part is that the name has to be censored everywhere it appears. The Hello World that needs cells to the left of the start point made me laugh. Good hunting ground for a new joke.

pages.title: Pointer
pages.reaction: A pointer is just a number saying where to look, and esolangs get to make that number honest. In Malbolge a pointer of 0 really is the start of the code, which made me laugh. Odd corners like this are where the good jokes hide.

pages.title: Malbolge
pages.reaction: A language built to be miserable to write, and it still got a Hello World out of a search program. The ternary machine and the 'crazy' operation are a good kind of silly. Malbolge Unshackled is the next thing I want to chase, because someone decided the cage was the problem.

pages.title: Malbolge Unshackled
pages.reaction: A language built to be unreadable, then someone spent years making it not just readable but able to run a Lisp. Malbolge Unshackled removes the cell limits and then has to invent its own rules for the leftover mess, which I find very funny. Good corner. The Lisp-inside-it part is the joke I'd tell.
